The symmetry of the ground state, S^2 = 0, Kx = Ky = 0, is preserved in the trial wave function used in CP/SYM and RC/SYM. The UHF trial wave function is generated with U = 0.5 as has been done before. (...) The RC results in Table II are essentially exact ground-state energies. || From a converged CP calculation, one can release the constraint (...) CP calculations will scale as a low power of the system size; FP and RC will of course have exponential scaling from the sign problem, albeit at a much reduced level with the proposed symmetry improvements. || Cost statements exist only for other calculations in the paper: Fig. 2 (FP, 8x8, N_up = N_dn = 32, U = 8, Hartree-Fock trial wave function): "The number of walkers was 10^5, with a total 20 separate runs to obtain the final averages and estimate the error bars."; Fig. 3 (FP, 4x4, N_up = N_dn = 7, U = 8): "The number of walkers is 5 x 10^5, with total 100 separate runs to estimate the error bars."; Fig. 4 (FP, periodic 8x8, N_up = N_dn = 13, U = 4): "The run took ~ 17 hours on 100 AMD Opteron 2.4GHz cores."; Fig. 5 (RC, 4x4, N_up = N_dn = 7, U = 8): "The number of walkers is 1 x 10^5, with total 100 runs in the RC portion to collect statistics."; Sec. III C example: "CPMC has 10,000 walkers, with back-propagation beta = 1." || We also acknowledge a DOE CMCSN award for facilitating stimulating interactions, and an INCITE award for computing using resources of the Oak Ridge Leadership Computing Facility at the Oak Ridge National Laboratory.

compute.reported_as: Energy results achieved by wave-functions before and after a Lanczos step are evaluated with the MC sample number in the magnitude of O(4.5×10^4). [Sec. III] ... (1) With a sample size of O(4.5×10^4), the step size is initially set to 2×10^−3 and then reduced to 2×10^−4. (2) With a sample size of O(4.5×10^4), the step size is initially set to 2×10^−3, the sample size is then increased to O(4.5×10^5) while maintaining the step size, and finally, the step size is reduced to 2×10^−4. ... For lattices larger than 64 sites, both strategies require no more than 2×10^4 optimization steps to achieve full convergence. [Sec. III.A] ... X. Liang thanks Eric J. Walter for resource allocations on the William & Mary Sciclone cluster. The author acknowledges William & Mary Research Computing and the Texas Advanced Computing Center (TACC) at The University of Texas at Austin for providing computational resources that have contributed to the results reported within this paper. Part of numerical results were obtained on the Bridges-2 at Pittsburgh Supercomputing Center through allocation (phy240244). [Sec. V Acknowledgement]
